summary: This document defines extensions to the Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol so it can set up different types of Layer 2 VPNs in a unified way. It builds on the L2TP model in which a session connects two Layer 2 circuits attached to peering L2TP access concentrators.

eli5.summary: A tunnel can join two separate private networks as if they shared one cable. This adds the settings needed so such tunnels can be set up in one consistent way.

questions: what is a pseudowire in l2tp
what is an attachment group identifier
how does l2tp detect a pseudowire tie
subtitle: How L2TP sets up pseudowires between provider edge devices so different kinds of Layer 2 VPNs can share one signaling method.

tldr.problem: Different Layer 2 VPN types (simple cross-connects, VPLS, VPWS) need to bind customer circuits across a provider network, and L2TP had no common way to name the endpoints.
tldr.mechanism: It adds a forwarder identifier made of a group ID and an individual ID, three new AVPs (AGI, Local End ID, Interface MTU), three new disconnect codes, and a procedure with tie detection.
tldr.outcome: L2TP signaling can now build L2VPNs in a unified way, using the incoming-call procedures to establish each pseudowire.

today: RFC 4667 is a Proposed Standard from September 2006. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and Reference Model
sections.content:
L2TPv3 (RFC 3931) can carry many Layer 2 protocols, where RFC 2661 supported only PPP. An L2TP Access Concentrator (LAC) cross-connects attachment circuits and L2TP sessions. L2VPN applications typically use this LAC-LAC reference model. This RFC covers what L2VPN applications have in common when they use L2TPv3 for signaling.

In the L2VPN framework a LAC is a Provider Edge (PE) device and the remote systems are Customer Edge (CE) devices. Each L2TP session acts as an emulated circuit, or pseudowire, that binds two forwarders together.
sections.eli5: A tunnel joins two doors in two far-away buildings. The building owners are the providers, and the people inside are the customers.

sections.title: Forwarders and Forwarder Identifiers
sections.content:
What a forwarder is depends on the application. In a simple cross-connect, an attachment circuit is bound one-to-one to a pseudowire. With Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS), a Virtual Switching Instance is a forwarder that connects to one or more circuits and pseudowires, and it does an extra lookup to decide where to send traffic. With Virtual Private Wire Service (VPWS), circuits are grouped into colored pools, and each pool is a forwarder.

Each forwarder on a PE gets an identifier unique on that PE, written <AGI, AII>. The Attachment Group Identifier (AGI) groups forwarders for signaling. The Attachment Individual Identifier (AII) tells forwarders in a group apart. To connect two forwarders, both MUST have the same AGI. The source forwarder's AII is the SAII and the target's is the TAII. For signaling, the identifier is just an arbitrary string of bytes, and values are up to the implementation.
sections.eli5: Every door gets a two-part name: which group it belongs to, and which door it is in that group. Two doors can only be joined if they are in the same group.

sections.title: AVPs and Result Codes
sections.content:
The signaling uses the incoming call procedures and these control messages: SCCRQ, SCCRP, ICRQ, ICRP, ICCN and SLI. Existing AVPs from RFC 3931 are reused: Router ID, Pseudowire Capabilities List, Pseudowire Type, L2-Specific Sublayer, Circuit Status and Remote End Identifier. The Remote End ID carries the TAII.

Three AVPs are new. The AGI AVP (type 89) groups a forwarder, and if it is omitted or has zero length the default AGI applies. Local End ID (type 90) carries the SAII, and if omitted it is assumed equal to the TAII. Interface MTU (type 91) is a 2-octet value, and if advertised in both directions the values MUST be identical, otherwise the pseudowire SHOULD NOT be established. All three MAY be hidden, and the M bit SHOULD be 0. Setting it to 1 would harm interoperability.

Three new CDN result codes were added: 23 mismatching interface MTU, 24 attempt to connect to a non-existent forwarder, and 25 attempt to connect to an unauthorized forwarder.
sections.eli5: The new notes say which group a door is in, which door is asking, and how big a package can be. Three new refusal reasons explain why a request was turned down.

sections.title: Signaling and Tie Detection
sections.content:
The two PEs first set up a control connection. Each lists its supported pseudowire types in the Pseudowire Capabilities List, and a PE SHOULD NOT start a session of a type the peer did not advertise. A PE then sends an ICRQ carrying the AGI, SAII and TAII. The receiver checks that it has a forwarder with that identifier and that the remote one is allowed to connect. If both hold, it replies with an ICRP, and otherwise with a CDN using code 24 or 25. The initiator then sends an ICCN.

Both PEs might start a pseudowire to each other at once. Each PE detects this tie by checking whether the received TAII and SAII match the SAII and TAII it sent, with any AGI prepended first. The standard L2TP tie-breaking procedure from RFC 3931 then removes the duplicate.
sections.eli5: One side knocks and says which door it wants. If that door exists and the visitor is allowed, the other side opens it. If both knock at once, a tie-break rule picks one knock.

sections.title: The Generic Algorithm
sections.content:
Each PE builds a SOURCE_FORWARDERS list of its local forwarders in a VPN. It also builds a TARGET_FORWARDERS list of the local forwarders to interconnect plus the remote forwarders of the same VPN. Both lists may come from manual configuration or auto-discovery. The algorithm sets up a full mesh between them.

For each pair: if the Router IDs differ, a pseudowire is needed. It is skipped if one is already established, and otherwise the PE opens a control connection if needed and sends an ICRQ. If the Router IDs match and the identifiers are equal, nothing is done. If they differ, the PE makes a local cross-connect. The rest handles the response (ICRP or CDN), an incoming ICRQ with tie detection, and binding the forwarder to the pseudowire once accepted.
sections.eli5: For every pair of doors, ask: are they in the same building? If so, just connect them. If not, build a tunnel unless one already exists.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The RFC adds no security considerations beyond those in RFC 3931 and the L2VPN framework (RFC 4664).

IANA assigned AVP values 89, 90 and 91 and CDN result codes 23, 24 and 25, following the registry procedure of RFC 3931.
sections.eli5: It adds no new safety worries of its own. The new labels simply got official numbers.

messages.label: ICRQ
messages.note: Carries AGI, Local End ID (SAII) and Remote End ID (TAII).

messages.label: ICRP
messages.note: Accepts if the forwarder exists and the connection is allowed.

messages.label: ICCN
messages.note: Local PE binds the source forwarder to the pseudowire.
